div.div:
npm before v3 (nested dependencies): - Before npm v3, dependencies were nested exactly according to the dependency graph.
Problems with npm v2
Lots of duplicate packages.
Deeply nested node_modules.
Windows often hit the MAX_PATH limit because paths became extremely long.

div.div:
npm v3+ (flattened): -
Starting with npm v3, npm tried to hoist as many dependencies as possible to the top level node_modules folder.
This solved the deep nesting problem, but introduced the phantom dependency problem because your app could now accidentally access picocolors.
Phantom dependency mean that package was installed by the some other dependency package of our project, but because now after the npm v3 onward, all the packages are installed on the top level node_modules folder, we can also directly use that dependency installed package, without the name of that package in dependency in our project package.json
So now the problem will arise when we willl uninstall our project dependency package, now becuase we using this dependency installed package in our project, we will get package not found error, becuase this dependency installed package was also uninstalled with our project dependency package
